facts.value: All researched psychological traits are influenced by both genes and environment, to varying degrees. These two sources of influence are often confounded in observational research of individuals and families.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: An example of this confounding can be shown in the transmission of depression from a depressed mother to her offspring. A theory based on environmental transmission would hold that an offspring, by virtue of their having a problematic rearing environment managed by a depressed mother, is at risk for developing depression.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: A hereditarian theory would hold that biological parents' genes affect depression risk in an offspring. Genes and environment are completely confounded in these simple transmission models.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Behavioral genetics researchers have employed methodologies that help to disentangle this confound and understand the nature and origins of individual differences in behavior. Traditionally, the research has involved twin studies and adoption or cross-fostering studies.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Gene-focused research has contributed to understanding genetic contributions to the development of psychological traits.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: The availability of microarray molecular genetic or genome sequencing technologies allows researchers to measure participant DNA variation directly.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Researchers test whether individual genetic variants within genes are associated with psychological traits and psychopathology through methods including genome-wide association studies.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: One goal of such research is similar to that in positional cloning: once a causal gene is discovered, biological research can be conducted to understand how that gene influences the phenotype.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: A major result of genetic association studies is the finding that psychological traits and psychopathology are highly polygenic, where a large number of genetic variants contribute to individual differences in the behavioral trait or propensity to the disorder.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Active research continues to work toward understanding the genetic and environmental bases of behavior and their interaction.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick

facts.value: Psychology encompasses many subfields and includes different approaches to the study of mental processes and behavior.
facts.programme_association: Psychology and Sociology - BA | University of Limerick
